title: silent-window-detector-and-operator-hint-cli
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add a detector that identifies low-activity windows ('silent windows') where alerting coverage should be evaluated; provides an operator CLI to collect minimal diagnostic bundles and suggested playbook hints. Backwards-compatible, no runtime changes to consumers.
description:
Motivation: On-call teams have reported recurrent blindspots during planned low-traffic windows (maintenance, regional holidays, cron quiet periods) where existing alert rules either flood with noisy infra signals or produce no coverage for regressions in background telemetry. This PR adds a lightweight 'silent window detector' that analyzes time-series metadata and alert history to (1) surface candidate windows with unusually low alert signal but nontrivial metric drift and (2) recommend focused diagnostic payloads an operator can collect with a single CLI command.

What this PR contains: checklist: - add silent-window-detector module with heuristics based on alert event rate, metric variance, and scheduled maintenance calendar - add operator hint CLI (slo-toolkit hint-collect) that bundles traces, recent metric snapshots, and a minimal sanitized logs sample - telemetry-lint rules that warn about missing synthetic probes or missing alert coverage during identified windows - integration tests and e2e harness for a simulated quiet window - docs and a short runbook template for on-call responders to use when a silent window is flagged

Design notes: The detector runs as an offline job (daily or ad-hoc) using existing metric and alert event APIs; it emits a compact JSON signal that can be consumed by the Console or by automation. Heuristics are tunable via a config map (defaults handle hourly/day-of-week patterns). The operator CLI uses the same credentials as existing oncall tooling and produces a tarball with a deterministic filename and a checksum for easy upload to postmortem artifacts. No hot path change to the production alerting runtime.

Commits summary: - Add detector core + config and unit tests (A. Patel) - Implement hint-collect CLI and unit test harness (A. Patel) - Add telemetry-lint rules and examples (R. Gupta) - Add docs + runbook templates (T. Rivera) - Fix: sanitize sensitive keys in bundled logs (security follow-up)

Files of interest (high level): - pkg/detector/silent_window_detector.go - pkg/detector/config.go - cmd/hint-collect/main.go - tooling/telemetry-lint/rules/silent_window_rules.yaml - docs/ops/silent-windows-runbook.md - test/e2e/silent_window_simulation_test.go - Makefile entries to wire daily job

Testing performed: Unit tests for heuristics covering edge cases (holiday days, maintenance windows, high variance microbursts). E2E simulated replay of 30 days with deterministic random seed to validate detection precision/recall thresholds. Manual smoke-run of hint-collect against staging cluster with sanitized artifact upload to S3. CI initially failed on lint (line-length and vet issues) and on a flaky test; fixed and retriggered, final CI green.

Review conversation: Reviewer Diego Morales: "Can you clarify how the detector differentiates a true quiet window from a transient alert suppression? Concerned about false positives during autoscaler events." Author reply: "Detector uses both alert event rate and metric variance over a rolling 72h window and ignores windows that overlap scheduled autoscaler maintenance (we already read cluster-schedule metadata). Added a unit test for autoscaler overlap." Reviewer Rina Gupta: "Please ensure the CLI does not include any PII tokens; what credential paths are used?" Author reply: "CLI explicitly strips known headers and secrets from logs and only reads K8s service account token via in-cluster recommended path; documented in the CLI README. Added a sanitizer step that removes Authorization and Cookie headers." Reviewer Tomás Rivera: "Docs look good; can we add a sample Linear ticket template for followup?" Author reply: "Added a template and integrated it into docs/silent-windows-runbook.md." Approvals: Diego Morales approved after autoscaler test fix; Rina approved after sanitization step; Tomás approved docs.

Risk and rollout: Low-risk. Detector runs offline as an opt-in job to start; the default config will only surface candidates above a conservative confidence threshold. Rollout plan: feature gated (config flag off by default) -> enable for two internal namespaces -> enable for internal SRE teams -> gradual expose in Console UI. No data migrations required.

Migration notes: Operators can opt-in by adding a configmap entry; hint-collect CLI is backwards compatible and does not change existing artifact formats beyond adding a single metadata file (silent_window_summary.json).

CI history: initial pipeline (linux/unit, linux/e2e, lint) failed on lint and a flaky e2e test; author fixed issues in two follow-ups and re-ran CI. Final status: all checks passing.

Merge: Squash merge after approvals and green CI.

Related: references ENG-4921 for scheduling metadata support and SRE-233 for on-call fatigue interviews.

Notes for release: include runbook in internal docs site and announce on #sre; add a short demo in the weekly oncall sync.
notes: This PR purposefully targets tooling that augments human on-call workflows rather than automated auto-remediation to reduce risk; follow-up planned to wire detector signals into the Console as an opt-in alerting 'insight' card.
